QUDT repository classification context

Context version: qudt-repository-context-v1.0.1

Purpose:
This context supports issue classification only. It helps determine issue type, area, likely effort, impact, and need for human review.
It is not sufficient by itself to determine whether a proposed ontology or vocabulary change is technically correct.

QUDT scope:
QUDT provides semantic specifications and reference data for
- quantities
- units of measure
- quantity kinds
- dimensions and dimension vectors
- prefixes
- constants
- systems of units
- data types
- mappings and interoperability
- related ontology and validation structures

Repository sources

The primary RDF sources are located under:
src/main/rdf

Schema

The main QUDT schema source of truth is:
src/main/rdf/schema/shacl/SCHEMA_QUDT_NoOWL.ttl

The corresponding OWL schema is derived into:
src/main/rdf/schema/SCHEMA_QUDT.ttl

The datatype schema source of truth is:
src/main/rdf/schema/shacl/SCHEMA_QUDT-DATATYPES_NoOWL.ttl

The corresponding OWL datatype schema is derived into:
src/main/rdf/schema/SCHEMA_QUDT-DATATYPE.ttl

The coordinate schema source of truth is:
src/main/rdf/schema/shacl/SCHEMA_QUDT-COORDINATES_NoOWL.ttl

The corresponding OWL coordinate schema is derived into:
src/main/rdf/schema/SCHEMA_QUDT-COORDINATES.ttl

When a corresponding SHACL source exists, do not treat the derived OWL file as the primary editing authority.

Schema issues may concern:

- classes
- properties
- domains and ranges
- ontology patterns
- SHACL shapes
- constraint definitions
- inference semantics
- backwards compatibility
- schema derivation

Schema and ontology-pattern changes are generally effort/large and often require ai/needs-human-review.

Vocabularies

Vocabulary sources are organised under src/main/rdf/vocab and include areas such as:

- units
- quantity kinds
- quantities
- dimension vectors
- prefixes
- constants
- systems of units
- types
- coordinates

Vocabulary-content issues include:

- missing or incorrect units
- quantity kinds
- quantities
- dimensions and dimension vectors
- symbols
- conversion multipliers and offsets
- prefixes
- constants
- labels
- mappings
- applicable units
- factor units
- scaling relationships
- systems of units

These issues are normally area/content.

Adding or changing an ontology or vocabulary entity normally requires at least effort/medium because the change must be checked against modelling conventions, existing entities, inference, and validation.

Validation and QA

Relevant validation and QA sources include:

src/main/rdf/validation/QUDT_SRC_QA_TESTS.ttl
src/main/rdf/validation/COLLECTION_QUDT_QA_TESTS_ALL.ttl
src/main/rdf/validation/COLLECTION_QUDT_USER_TESTS.ttl

Schema SHACL files also contain constraints.

Validation issues may concern:

- incorrect or missing constraints
- SHACL violations or warnings
- unexpected validation results
- deprecated properties or instances
- integrity of QUDT ontology sources
- user-facing validation behaviour

A problem in the semantic rule itself is usually area/content.

A problem in how validation is executed, reported, or integrated into CI is usually area/tooling.

Build, inference, and repository tooling

The QUDT build uses Maven and configuration in pom.xml together with supporting files under:

src/build

The build performs activities including:

- RDF validation
- inference
- merging inferred triples
- RDF formatting
- source inspection
- schema derivation
- release packaging

Important inferred relationships include:

qudt:applicableUnit
qudt:hasFactorUnit
qudt:scalingOf

Tooling issues may concern:

- pom.xml
- src/build
- SPARQL queries
- Groovy scripts
- GitHub Actions
- CI execution
- release scripts
- formatting
- packaging
- converters
- generated outputs

These issues are generally area/tooling unless the underlying cause is incorrect ontology or vocabulary content.

Documentation

Important checked-in documentation includes:

README.md
BUILDING.md
CHANGELOG.md

README.md describes the repository, QUDT distributions, loading options, and user versus contributor validation.

BUILDING.md describes build processes, schema source-of-truth rules, inference, validation, and contributor workflows.

CHANGELOG.md records historical and recent changes. Treat it as evidence of earlier decisions and recent work, not as the current source of truth.

Documentation-only issues are area/documentation.

Community and submissions

Community extensions and contributed material may be located under:

src/main/rdf/community
src/main/rdf/submissions

An issue limited to a community extension normally has narrower impact than an issue affecting the core schema or core vocabularies.

Impact considerations

Issues are more likely to be impact/high when they concern:

- incorrect conversions or dimensions
- incorrect commensurability
- broadly used units or quantity kinds
- core schema semantics
- incorrect inference
- validation that allows incorrect released data
- breaking changes
- interoperability with widely used standards
- changes affecting many entities or downstream consumers

Issues are more likely to be impact/medium when they concern:

- one specialised domain
- one vocabulary group
- one external mapping
- one community extension
- a limited contributor workflow
- a narrowly scoped validation rule

Issues are more likely to be impact/low when they concern:

- spelling
- wording
- broken links
- display-only issues
- isolated documentation improvements
- local cosmetic inconsistencies

Evidence limitations

The supplied file map and documentation excerpts are not the complete repository.

Do not infer that an entity or feature is absent merely because it does not appear in the supplied context.

When determining whether an issue is factually correct would require examining RDF entities, mappings, validation reports, or build output that have not been supplied, include ai/needs-human-review.
